To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the texture features of Gabor, fractal dimensions and 59 bin LBP are the top performers in distinguishing between benign and malignant ovarian masses; 2. a combination of the top 3 texture features can achieve an accuracy level of up to 90%.
the Gabor filter and 256 bin L B P texture features are the most effective features for distinguishing benign and malignant ovarian masses.

the texture features of the Gabor filters are the most effective in classifying benign and malignant ovarian masses, and that combining the classification results of a small number of the best performing features improves the accuracy of the diagnosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparative evaluation of the performance of the image texture features in distinguishing benign from malignant ovarian masses.
the development of an effective and efficient texture feature based automated diagnostic support system for B mode ultrasound images.

the development of automated diagnostic systems for medical images, and in particular, for ultrasound images of ovarian masses, with the goal of assisting radiologists in their diagnosis of ovarian masses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gabor filter texture feature is the most effective among the investigated features for this task.
the texture features that are based on Gabor filter and fractal dimensions perform better in distinguishing benign from malignant ovarian masses than the rest.
no single texture feature can be claimed to be superior to others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of texture features can be used to achieve a level of accuracy of 90% in discriminating benign from malignant ovarian masses.
a combination of the seven investigated texture features provides a better overall classification accuracy than the individual texture features.

a combination of the best performing texture features is likely to be a better option than the best performing single texture feature for automated diagnostic support of ultrasound scan of the ovaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simple majority rule based combination of the top k performing features can further boost the performance of the classification systems based on any of the individual texture features.

a simple majority voting rule based decision level fusion of the classification results of individual texture features can improve the overall classification accuracy by up to 5% without the need for more sophisticated feature selection or fusion schemes.
a combination of these features provides a more reliable support for the diagnostic task.
